title: Two different records with the same name and subtitle
author: mykhailopylyp
summary: PowerToys Run still keys user-selected history by Result.ToString, which is only Title plus SubTitle, so distinct executables with identical display text share ranking history.
next_action: Approve a stable per-result identity design that distinguishes executable path and plugin while migrating existing history safely.

confidence.rationale: The current collision mechanism is directly visible in source.

judgment.rationale: The issue's proposed path-based identity remains consistent with current source: UserSelectedRecord uses result.ToString as the dictionary key and Result.ToString formats only title and subtitle.
evidence: Maintainer discussion confirms different executables may legally have the same title and subtitle.
Current UserSelectedRecord.Add, Remove, and GetSelectedData use result.ToString as the key.
Current Result.ToString returns only Title and SubTitle.
UserSelectedRecordItem already stores IconPath and PluginID, providing migration context but not unique identity.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a stable per-result identity design that distinguishes executable path and plugin while migrating existing history safely.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run still keys user-selected history by Result.ToString, which is only Title plus SubTitle, so distinct executables with identical display text share ranking history.
known_information: Different programs and shortcuts can share title and subtitle.
Current records store title, subtitle, icon path, plugin ID, and search text.
inferences: A canonical path plus plugin identity should distinguish the reported program cases, but non-file plugins need their own stable identity contract.
issue_context.analysis: The defect is current and source-localized enough for a queued design, with migration and non-file result identity called out as required safeguards.
initial_investigation: Confirmed all selection-history operations still use Result.ToString.

actions.label: Approve stable Run history identity
actions.design_summary: Replace Title+SubTitle history keys with a plugin-aware stable result identity and migrate legacy records.
actions.note: Approval would start a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight pass writes no code or upstream content.

proposed_fixes.title: Key Run selection history by stable result identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: UserSelectedRecord collapses distinct results because its dictionary key is Result.ToString, and Result.ToString contains only title and subtitle.
plan: Add a stable history identity supplied by each result/plugin, using canonical executable or shortcut path plus PluginID where available.
Use that identity consistently in Add, Remove, and GetSelectedData, retaining a legacy Title/SubTitle lookup only for one-time migration.
Add collision tests with two results sharing title/subtitle but pointing to different executables and verify independent counts and ordering.
verification: Launch two identically named results from different paths and confirm their selection counts remain independent across restart.
Load an existing UserSelectedRecord.json and confirm usable legacy history is migrated without corrupting the file.

confidence.rationale: The key collision is explicit in both the issue and current source; migration details are the primary implementation risk.
